entities.summary:
Wojciech of Jastrzębiec was a prominent Polish mediaeval politician and religious leader, whose significance lies in his role as a bishop of Cracow and Poznań, and his involvement in the royal court of Władysław II of Poland.




He was born in 1362 in Łubnice and died in 1436, leaving behind a legacy as a key figure in the governance and religious landscape of medieval Poland.




As a bishop, Wojciech played a crucial role in shaping the religious and political discourse of his time, and his influence extended beyond his diocese, impacting the wider region of Eastern Europe.
